nrIncident.summary: Disruption in the Barking area until at least 05:00 on Friday 30 October: amended Suffragette line service, and no trains between Barking and Grays via Rainham (Essex)
nrIncident.routes:
c2c between London Fenchurch Street and Grays / Laindon / Pitsea / Leigh-on-Sea / Southend Central / Thorpe Bay / Shoeburyness, and also between Barking and Grays / Southend Central
London Overground between Gospel Oak and Barking Riverside
nrIncident.message:
A freight train has derailed between Woodgrange Park and Barking, blocking some lines.
Some trains through Barking will be cancelled or revised as a result. Where trains do run there may be delays of up to 10 minutes in the area.
• London Overground are running a reduced service on the Suffragette line between Gospel Oak and South Tottenham. No trains will run between South Tottenham and Barking Riverside - please note a points failure at South Tottenham means services between Upper Holloway and South Tottenham may be cancelled or revised
• There will be no c2c service between Barking and Grays via Dagenham Dock, Rainham (Essex) and Purfleet
Disruption is expected until at least 05:00 on Friday 30 October.
c2c customer advice:
What's happened?
A freight train has derailed between Woodgrange Park and Barking, which means platforms 7 and 8 at Barking station are blocked.
How does this affect my journey?
No services are calling at Dagenham Dock, Rainham or Purfleet. Please expect delays and service alterations.
Your ticket will be accepted at no extra cost on:
• First Essex buses between Purfleet and Grays
• Greater Anglia between London Liverpool Street and Southend Victoria
• London Buses between Barking, Dagenham Dock, Rainham, Purfleet and Grays
• London Buses Superloop SL12
• London Buses EL2 for Dagenham Dock
• London Underground District line between Barking and Upminster, and Jubilee line between West Ham and Stratford (London)
Replacement buses are running half hourly between between Upminster and Grays, calling at Rainham, Purfleet, Grays.
What should I do?
Please check before you travel and allow extra time for your journey. c2c are working to keep customers moving and will provide details of any alternative travel arrangements as soon as they are confirmed.
London Overground customer advice:
Service is suspended between South Tottenham and Barking Riverside.
Alterations to services:
• Services will depart Gospel Oak at XX:09 and XX:39
• Services will depart South Tottenham at XX:13 and XX:43
Your ticket can be used, at no extra cost on the following services:
• Elizabeth line via any reasonable route
• London Buses via any reasonable route
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey for today using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner. For journeys on Tuesday 27 October and beyond please check back later.
For helpful advice if you need to travel on a rail replacement service, including accessibility and bicycle information, please use our Rail Replacement Services page.
You can find the pick-up and drop-off location of rail replacement services by checking station signage or by searching for your station on our Find a Station page.
Please be advised that replacement vehicles may be busier than usual, and you should allow extra time for your journey.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

nrIncident.summary: Storm Boelo - disruption to ScotRail some services expected until the end of Tuesday 27 October
nrIncident.routes: Various routes across the ScotRail network
nrIncident.message:
A yellow weather warning for strong winds remains in place across most of Scotland. This will affect journeys on some ScotRail routes until the end of the day on Tuesday 27 October. Some routes also remain affected following Storm Boelo which brought heavy rain and high winds across the weekend.
Disruption is expected until the end of the day on Tuesday 27 October.
Tuesday 27 October:
Planned alterations are in place on the routes listed below, however you should check before you travel on any route in case of short notice alterations.
Between Glasgow Queen Street and Oban
Some trains will be revised to start or finish at different stations or cancelled in full as stated below. Any trains that do run may be subject to delays or short notice alterations:
• 05:17 Oban to Glasgow Queen Street will terminate at Dalmally. A replacement coach will operate from Oban calling at all stops to Crianlarich then drop off as required to Glasgow.
• 05:20 Glasgow Queen Street to Oban will terminate at Arrochar and Tarbet. A replacement coach will operate from Arrochar to Oban calling at all stations.
• An additional train service will start at Dalmally to Oban. This service will depart at 07:51.
• An additional train service will start at Arrochar & Tarbet. This train will depart at 07:10.
• 10:36 Glasgow Queen Street to Oban is cancelled. Customers should travel on 12:22 Glasgow Queen Street to Oban.
• 14:41 Oban to Glasgow Queen Street will be cancelled. Customers should travel on 18:24 Oban to Glasgow Queen Street.
Between Glasgow Queen Street and Mallaig:
Trains on this route may be delayed or revised.
Between Inverness and Kyle of Lochalsh / Wick:
Trains on this route may be delayed by up to 20 minutes.
Ticket flexibility:
If you have a ticket dated Saturday 24, Sunday 25 or Monday 26 October and postponed your travel, you can use it to travel at no extra cost on services on Tuesday 27 October.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey for today using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
For helpful advice if you need to travel on a rail replacement service, including accessibility and bicycle information, please use our Rail Replacement Services page.
You can find the pick-up and drop-off location of rail replacement services by checking station signage or by searching for your station on our Find a Station page.
Please be advised that replacement vehicles may be busier than usual, and you should allow extra time for your journey.
